disease_name: Duchenne muscular dystrophy due to a nonsense (premature termination) variant in DMD exon 55
causal_defect: Hemizygous loss-of-function point mutation in DMD (Xp21.2) creating a premature termination codon in exon 55, an exon in the distal part of the central rod/spectrin-repeat domain. Nonsense variants are a well-documented, recurrent DMD mutation class (~10% of all DMD alleles; 726 nonsense mutations in 7,149 catalogued), with CGA>TGA hypermutability.
molecular_consequence: Premature termination codon in DMD exon 55 causing nonsense-mediated decay and/or a C-terminally truncated Dp427m that cannot anchor the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex; functional dystrophin is effectively absent at the sarcolemma.
key_cell_types: CNS neurons expressing Dp427c/Dp140 (exon 55 is upstream of the Dp71 promoter, so Dp71 is spared)
key_pathology: Contraction-induced sarcolemmal microtears with calcium influx and mitochondrial calcium overload
Repeated necrosis-regeneration cycles leading to satellite cell exhaustion
Chronic innate immune infiltration and TGF-beta-driven endomysial fibrosis with fatty replacement
Progressive dilated cardiomyopathy and respiratory muscle failure as the dominant causes of death
evidence_strength: Strong for the gene-disease relationship and for the dystrophin-deficiency cascade (large genotype-phenotype cohorts; decades of mdx/canine model work). Weak for anything specific to exon 55: I retrieved no exon-55-specific mechanistic or therapeutic literature within budget, so exon-55 claims are inference from the reading-frame rule and dystrophin domain architecture.
major_unknowns: Whether this specific exon 55 PTC triggers efficient NMD versus producing a stable truncated protein — this determines whether readthrough (e.g. ataluren-class) has a substrate at all and should be measured directly in patient myotubes or urine-derived cells

Whether exon 55 is dispensable: skipping a single in-frame exon would not restore frame, so a multi-exon skip (or readthrough) strategy is required — the minimal skippable block around exon 55 and the functionality of the resulting dystrophin are untested
Residual dystrophin level in this patient's muscle (any trace expression strongly modifies progression)
Whether brain isoform involvement (Dp140 loss) contributes to the cognitive phenotype in this genotype stratum
Degree of pre-existing fibrosis/fat replacement, which caps the benefit of any dystrophin-restoring approach

key_evidence.statement: DMD is the causal gene for Duchenne muscular dystrophy; Monarch resolves the disease to MONDO:0010679, described as progressive muscle weakness and wasting from degeneration of skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle.

In a cohort of 1,111 DMD mutations (891 with phenotype), 506 were point mutations including 294 nonsense mutations; CGA>TGA sites are uniformly hypermutable, and nonsense variants are associated with the severe Duchenne rather than Becker phenotype.

In 7,149 DMD mutations in the TREAT-NMD global database, 726 (50% of small mutations, ~10% overall) were nonsense mutations, confirming this is a sizeable and clinically recognized stratum rather than a one-off.

A premature termination codon in exon 55 is expected to abolish translation of the cysteine-rich and C-terminal domains, which mediate beta-dystroglycan and syntrophin binding, so even any escaping truncated product should be non-functional as a mechanical linker.

Because exon 55 lies within the central rod domain and single-exon skipping would not restore the reading frame disrupted by a PTC, readthrough of the PTC (or a multi-exon skip that excises exon 55 in frame) is the mechanistically coherent restoration strategy; the single-exon-skipping paradigm used for deletion patients does not transfer directly.

The PTC in exon 55 may be efficiently degraded by nonsense-mediated decay, leaving too little mRNA template for a readthrough agent to act on; this would predict non-response to readthrough therapy and is directly testable by measuring DMD transcript abundance and allele-specific decay in patient-derived myotubes.

No exon-55-specific mechanistic, readthrough-amenability or multi-exon-skip study was retrieved; PubMed queries returned largely unrelated MET exon 14 oncology literature, so absence of findings here is a retrieval limitation and not evidence against these approaches.

conclusion_note: Upstream mechanism (dystrophin loss) is established with high confidence, so the disease model needed for therapeutic reasoning is solid. However, the exon-55-specific layer — NMD efficiency, readthrough amenability, and whether any multi-exon skip restores frame — is not established in the literature I retrieved and must be resolved experimentally before committing to a modality. Budget was partly consumed by an off-target PubMed result set; a focused follow-up query on DMD nonsense readthrough and on multi-exon skipping around exons 50-56 would sharpen the modality choice.
